name: Botswana
headline: Botswana has a modern data law with an active regulator, but clinic and hospital systems do not share records and patients have no portal.

access.summary: The Data Protection Act 2024 gives a free copy of your data within one month, and the Public Health Act lets facilities only temporarily deny record access. There is no patient portal, and we quote the published Bill because the enacted text was not verified.
detail: Section 42 of the Data Protection Bill 2024, enacted as Act 18 of 2024 and in force from 14 January 2025, gives a right to confirm, access and get a copy of personal data. Further copies may carry a reasonable fee.
Section 38 sets a reply within one month, extendable by up to two months with the Commission's approval. The first answer is free. Electronic requests get electronic replies.
Section 139 of the Public Health Act 2013 deals with user and parent access to health records. The head of a facility may temporarily deny access if disclosure would seriously harm the user.

We found no national patient portal or app. Our clauses come from the published Bill. We did not open the enacted Act, so exact wording is not verified, which keeps the score in the lower half of its band.

control.summary: Health data may be processed without consent for diagnosis, treatment and health system management, and there is no shared record with sharing choices or an access log. Patients keep only general rights to object.
detail: Section 30 of the Data Protection Bill bans processing health data, then allows it with explicit consent or when needed for medical diagnosis, care, treatment or managing health services. The professional secrecy condition in section 30(3) attaches only to public health processing.
Section 48 lets a person object to processing based on public interest or legitimate interest, but the controller can continue with compelling legitimate grounds.

In November 2025 the Minister of Local Government told Parliament that the Patient Information Management System, Integrated Patient Management System, DHIS2 and ePulse are not interfaced to share data across facilities. With no shared record, there is no patient sharing setting or access log to use.

privacy.summary: The 2024 Act treats health as sensitive, requires breach notice within 72 hours and allows fines up to P50 million or 4% of turnover. With no health-sector cases found, this scores the general law, which the regulator enforced against a government portal in 2026.
detail: Section 63 requires notice to the Information and Data Protection Commission within 72 hours where feasible. Section 64 requires telling people when a breach is high risk. Section 83 sets fines up to P50 million or 4% of worldwide turnover.
The Act binds the State. In July 2026 the Commission issued an enforcement order that led the government to suspend its electronic payslip portal, Mmegi reported.
Section 8 says the President appoints the Commissioner on the Minister's advice. Section 144 of the Public Health Act makes falsifying or wrongly destroying health records an offence.
Botswana is outside the EU, so the EHDS does not apply. A five-year Data Sharing Agreement with the United States, signed with a health MoU on 23 December 2025, has terms we did not verify.

commercial.summary: People can object at any time to direct marketing, and the published Bill makes selling personal data a crime (enacted wording not verified). We found no rules on de-identified health data, health apps or brokers.
detail: Section 48 of the Data Protection Bill gives a right to object to direct marketing, including profiling. Once a person objects, the data may not be used for marketing.
DLA Piper reports that the Electronic Communications and Transactions Act 2014 requires an opt-out in every marketing message, with fines for those who keep sending after an opt-out.

Health data sits in the sensitive class under section 30, so commercial use needs explicit consent. Section 84(2) of the Bill makes selling personal data an offence (fine of P500,000 or up to nine years). We did not verify the enacted wording, so it does not raise the score. We found no rules on de-identified data, brokers or health apps.

journey.summary: Several electronic systems run in public facilities, but the government told Parliament in November 2025 they are not interfaced to share data. An electronic medical record was being piloted in two districts, with a health information exchange planned.
detail: The Ministry's health data collaborative says Botswana rolled out the Integrated Patient Management System to all public hospitals, alongside PIMS, OpenMRS and DHIS2. It calls them vertical systems that do not share data readily.
In November 2025 Parliament heard that 223 clinics were connected to the network, with 283 expected by the end of the financial year. An electronic medical record was being piloted in two districts.
Those systems are to link to a Botswana Health Information Exchange with a Master Patient Index covering public and private facilities. We found no date for that link.
The 2026/27 budget funds a digitalisation of health services project and a World Bank financed electronic stock system for medicines.

clinical.summary: A clinician cannot open a patient's record from another facility because systems are not interfaced. The Public Health Act requires each facility to keep a permanent record and protect it from unauthorised access.
detail: Section 141 of the Public Health Act requires each facility to keep a permanent health record for every user. Section 144 requires controls against unauthorised access.
Section 142 lets a provider examine records for treatment, study, teaching or research with the authorisation of the user, the head of facility and the ethics committee.

The government said in November 2025 that facility systems are not interfaced for access across facilities. The planned Master Patient Index would hold medical histories across public and private care, but it is not yet working.

research.summary: Research use of health records needs the patient's authorisation plus ethics committee approval under the Public Health Act, and the 2024 Act adds a right to object to research use. Safeguards earn the top of the no-opt-out band.
detail: Section 142 of the Public Health Act allows record use for study, teaching or research with authorisation of the user, the facility head and the ethics committee. Section 140 needs written authorisation before experimental treatment.
Section 30 of the Data Protection Bill allows sensitive data use for research with safeguards. Section 48(6) gives a right to object to research use unless it is in the public interest.
Section 144 makes falsifying, or creating or destroying a health record without authority, an offence. We found no public register of research data uses.

ai.summary: BoMRA's draft 2026 medical device regulations set rules for AI and machine learning devices, including bias checks and change control plans, but they are still in draft. No AI law exists, and the national AI policy is unfinished.
detail: Draft regulation 78 would require AI and machine learning devices to document model design, show training data quality and bias controls, prove clinical validation and run post-market monitoring. A predetermined change control plan would govern adaptive algorithms.
BoMRA said in August 2026 that the regulations under the Medicines and Related Substances Act 2025 were still drafts, presented to industry at a stakeholder forum.
Mandatory registration of high-risk (Class C and D) devices had a 30 June 2026 deadline under BoMRA's roadmap. The Probe reported in August 2026 that Botswana has no AI-specific law.
